newsitem.title: JAPAN: IATA says sees strong passenger growth in Asia.
newsitem.headline: IATA says sees strong passenger growth in Asia.

text.p: The International Air Transport Association (IATA) said on Tuesday it saw solid passenger traffic growth in the Asia-Pacific region, which it predicted would account for 50.5 percent of the global share by 2010.
This compared with its 26.4 percent share in 1985.

"Over the past 10 years, the Asia-Pacific region has put far more investment into airports than any other region of the world," said William Gaillard, IATA corporate communications director, adding that the region's investment totalled $200 billion.
Airport construction in China, for example, enjoyed the fastest growth in Asia and the world. Over the next 10 years, China was expected to build 20 airports at a cost of $5.5 billion, he said.
Peter Morris, the IATA's director of aviation information, told the same briefing the Asia-Pacific region would lead global growth in international passenger flights.
He said the IATA projected an average annual growth rate worldwide of 7.1 percent between 1996 and 2000, while that in Asia could be nearly 10 percent a year.
"Looking at the growth for the future, a very optimistic story arises in the Asia-Pacific region," Morris said.
